title: Message envelope v1
description: The envelope of Kafka events and RabbitMQ commands: the JSON object in the message body. $defs/Envelope is the open general form that a receiver relies on. Every message type has its own closed schema, in the file of its topic, built from the definitions below. Conventions are described in contracts/README.md.

Envelope.description: General form of any message. A receiver needs message_id, type, created_at and payload and ignores members it does not know, at any depth. traceparent is not described here on purpose: a message without it or with an invalid one is still accepted and starts a new trace.

headers.description: Cross-service headers from the list of the contract. A receiver reads only the ones it knows.

version.description: Version of the state of the message key, as in KeyVersion but open: a receiver ignores members it does not know here as well.

MessageId.description: Message id: UUID v7 in lowercase, the id of the outbox row. It stays the same when the message is sent again, and receivers drop duplicates by it.

MessageType.description: Message type: <area>.<name>.v<major>, for example booking.state.v1. For an event the area is the topic name without its version.

CreatedAt.description: Creation time of the outbox row by the service clock, in UTC, truncated to milliseconds when the row is created: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ. Delivery delays are measured from it, so unlike other moments in the contracts it keeps milliseconds.

ChangeId.description: Id of a change of the publisher: UUID v7, the same in all messages of one change, for example in the availability events of every date of a range.

PiiRetainUntil.description: Deadline for the personal data of the message, in UTC without a fraction of a second: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ. Every copy of the message erases its personal data at the earlier of this deadline and 30 days after created_at, and a receiver neither keeps nor uses them after it, even if the message arrives later. Only commands with personal data carry it; events never do.

Traceparent.description: W3C traceparent of the publisher, version 00. Its trace id is the correlation id.

EventHeaders.description: Headers of an event. Events carry no personal data, so there is no pii_retain_until.

KeyVersion.description: Version of the state of the message key. A receiver applies a message only if its version is higher than the stored one, comparing the epoch first and then the number; an equal version is a duplicate. number grows with every change of the key in the database of its owner and with every new publication of the key. epoch grows after that database is restored from a backup: the owner publishes a full snapshot of the new epoch, which wins over the older events of the same keys. Keys missing from the snapshot, the data lost by the restore, stay in the topic with the old epoch until the end of its retention, so meanwhile copies are rebuilt from the owner's export, not from the topic.
